baseline_arms: cuBLAS GEMV via torch.matmul (INT32 where supported, FP32 fallback otherwise; fallback is never silent and is recorded as dtype_fallback_reason in the per-shape entry).

cuBLASLt IMMA INT8 GEMM via torch._int_mm (INT8 inputs / INT32 accumulator). uTPU N=1 GEMV is padded to N=8 to satisfy IMMA alignment (N % 8 == 0). Per-N-column time (kernel_ms.median / N_padded) is reported as ms_per_n_column_median and is what the parent uses for gap_vs_cublaslt_int8_pct_median; this is the dtype-matched apples-to-apples GEMV comparison to the uTPU kernel.
TorchInductor nn.Linear in FP32 (framework reference, not a dtype-matched comparison; documented as such).
methodology.cublaslt_int8_alignment_caveat: cuBLASLt IMMA INT8 GEMM (torch._int_mm) requires N % 8 == 0 on Ampere/Ada/Hopper/Blackwell. A native N=1 INT8 GEMV does not exist in the IMMA path, so the subprocess pads the uTPU N=1 input to N=8 (the alignment minimum) and divides the wall time by N_padded to obtain a GEMV-equivalent per-column time. This is slightly favorable to cuBLAS (launch + tensor-core setup costs amortize across N_padded columns), and the gap reported as gap_vs_cublaslt_int8_pct_median uses this per-column figure — i.e. the most cuBLAS-favorable honest comparison available without inventing a non-existent IMMA N=1 GEMV. The per-shape entry preserves both kernel_ms (full N=8 wall time) and ms_per_n_column_median so a reader can see exactly how the gap was computed.
dtype_caveats: uTPU kernel: INT8 inputs, INT32 accumulator, INT4-quantised output (matches the FPGA datapath). Output quantisation is applied post-cuBLAS-equivalent GEMV and is included in the uTPU kernel_time_ms.

cuBLAS GEMV reference: the subprocess attempts INT32 inputs / INT32 accumulator via torch.matmul (apples-to-apples accumulator dtype with the uTPU kernel). Torch builds without an INT32 addmv/addmm CUDA kernel (observed on Torch 2.11+cu130 with the RTX 5070 sm_120) raise NotImplementedError and the subprocess falls back to FP32 inputs / FP32 accumulator via the standard cuBLAS GEMV path. The per-shape entry records the actual measured dtype in dtype_W/dtype_x/dtype_accum/dtype_out plus an explicit dtype_fallback_reason on the fallback path. The uTPU-vs-cuBLAS gap on the FP32-fallback path is not a dtype-matched comparison; for the dtype-matched answer see gap_vs_cublaslt_int8_pct_median (cuBLASLt IMMA INT8 GEMM via torch._int_mm).

cuBLASLt IMMA INT8 GEMM reference (dtype-matched): INT8 inputs / INT32 accumulator via torch._int_mm. uTPU N=1 GEMV is padded to N=8 (IMMA alignment minimum) and per-N-column time is used for the gap; this is the honest apples-to-apples GEMV comparison and removes the INT8-vs-FP32 dtype asterisk on the cuBLAS-FP32-fallback row. See cublaslt_int8_alignment_caveat in this methodology block for the exact derivation.

Inductor reference: FP32 nn.Linear compiled via torch.compile(backend='inductor', fullgraph=True). Same op semantics but FP32 dtype throughout. Recorded as a framework reference, not a dtype-matched comparison; gap_vs_inductor_pct is reported but the writeup flags this caveat explicitly.
methodology.isolation: cuBLAS + cuBLASLt IMMA + Inductor timings run in a separate Python process (_cublas_baseline_torch_subprocess.py) so the parent's NVRTC driver context for the uTPU kernel does not collide with Torch's CUDA / Inductor contexts (the same isolation pattern as inductor_oracle_subprocess.py).
methodology.rng_seed_per_shape: 0xC0DE XOR'd with M*1009 + K for the uTPU kernel; 0xC0DE / 0xACE / 0xCAB inside the Torch subprocess.
methodology.scope: Sim/host-measured. No physical-board claim. cuBLAS / cuBLASLt IMMA / Inductor numbers depend on the GPU + driver of the host that regenerates the artifact; uTPU numbers depend on NVRTC + cuda-python on the same host.
methodology.shape_set_description: Six fixed (M, K) shapes covering small (16x16) to medium-large (512x512) GEMV; N=1 in all cases (FC inference). Locked in firmware/host/run_cublas_baseline.py::SHAPES; changes to this list invalidate prior artifacts.
methodology.stability_protocol: v2 (spin-up + trimmed median). Each per-shape arm runs (a) one discarded spin-up pass of warmup + iters (engages GPU boost clocks and warms the lazy-load kernel cache before any timed sample is recorded), then (b) 7 counted back-to-back stability runs, each a fresh warmup + iters block with CUDA-event timing. The per-shape kernel_ms reports per_run_medians_ms (full N-long list, retained for diagnostics so the gate-failure print loop and the arms_exceeding_stability_threshold_pct field can surface the raw outlier values) AND per_run_medians_trimmed_ms — if num_stability_runs >= 4 the highest + lowest per-run median are dropped before computing both timing_stability_pct (CV = stddev / mean of the trimmed medians * 100) and the pooled samples used for the published kernel_ms.median (samples from dropped outlier runs are excluded from the shipped median, not just from the CV stat). The aggregate field max_timing_stability_pct_across_arms surfaces the worst inter-run CV across every populated (arm, shape) pair; the gate test asserts this is at or below 10.0% so no shipped median can claim 'stable' with a higher post-trim inter-run variance. This addresses two distinct noise classes: the +29.16% -> +4.92% cuBLAS-fallback median swing observed on the same RTX 5070 (wall-clock methodology artifact at GEMV scale — fixed by CUDA-event timing in v1) AND the single-outlier-run pattern observed on the first v1 regen on WSL2 + RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, e.g. cublaslt_int8 @ 128x128 = [59us, 9us, 9us] (one cold-clock or thermal-blip stray, two stable — fixed by the v2 spin-up + trimmed median pair). Background GPU load on the host can still defeat the gate; remediation on a gate failure is documented per-failure: bump --warmup / --iters / --num-stability-runs and re-run with no other GPU work on the box.
methodology.tflops_definition: 2 * M * N * K / median_kernel_ms * 1e-12. INT-MAC count for uTPU + cuBLAS / cuBLASLt IMMA INT8 (all INT32 accumulator); Inductor runs FP32 so its TFLOPS would not be comparable and is omitted.
methodology.timing_protocol: Per-iter timing uses CUDA events: torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) records are inserted in stream order around each call, then a single torch.cuda.synchronize() is issued after the iter loop and start.elapsed_time(end) (ms) gives the per-iter GPU time. This replaces the older wall-clock + per-iter-sync brackets — at GEMV scale (30-50us kernel time) the host-side sync overhead was the dominant noise source (~5-20us per sample, i.e. 15-40% of signal); CUDA events measure GPU execution directly with sub-us resolution. Warmup invocations are discarded. Reported per arm: mean, median, stdev, min, max, p95 (ms) over the full sample list.

cublas.dtype_fallback_reason: int32 cuBLAS matmul unsupported on this Torch+CUDA build (NotImplementedError: "addmv_impl_cuda" not implemented for 'Int'); fell back to fp32 cuBLAS GEMV (the standard PyTorch dispatch path).

cublaslt_int8.imma_unavailable_reason: M=16 <= 16; torch._int_mm requires M > 16 at the Python wrapper layer ("self.size(0) needs to be greater than 16"). This is a PyTorch dispatch constraint, not a hardware IMMA alignment constraint; shapes with M >= 17 (and in practice M >= 32 on the locked SHAPES grid) clear the wrapper and reach the actual cuBLASLt IMMA INT8 GEMM path. The (M=16, K=16) shape in the locked SHAPES grid will therefore stay IMMA-ineligible until either (a) M is widened past 16 in the shape set, or (b) the harness wires the raw cuBLASLt API instead of torch._int_mm.

inductor.dtype_caveat: Inductor reference runs in float32 (the default Torch dispatch path for nn.Linear); uTPU kernel runs INT8 inputs with INT32 accumulator. Not a like-for-like dtype comparison; see methodology block.
